chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who led a group in prayer and suffered from a nosebleed after he had prayed one or two rak'ahs, so he put forward a man from those who had missed one or two rak'ahs. He said: 'He completes the prayer with them, then puts forward another man and makes the prostration of salutation with them, and he himself stands and completes the remainder of his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What should an Imam do if he gets a nosebleed during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the specific scenario where an Imam's prayer is invalidated by a minor impurity (ru'af) occurring after the initial rak'ahs, necessitating a seamless transition of leadership. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Imam's personal prayer validity is distinct from his role as congregational leader, allowing him to remain in place to complete his own obligation while a deputy assumes the public leadership duties. This ensures the continuity of the congregational prayer without requiring the entire group to restart.
